We also want to understand any legal/accounting implications on passing credits or issuing vouchers to a third party sponsor. Leah (CFO) is cc'd.

Appreciate quick direction — demo is Thursday and sponsor asks for a path.

Neha / team,

Thanks for flagging — good, solvable ask but needs a short hop across pricing/legal/ops. High-level options from pricing: 

1) Promo credits (current model) — we can issue credits to a single onboarding account and redistribute via internal vouchers. Pros: fastest. Cons: credits are technically tied to customer account; transfer to third party (sponsor) or sponsor-directed allocation is tricky from legal/accounting.

2) Sponsored voucher (link-based voucher) — we can create vouchers the sponsor purchases or we issue on their behalf. Vouchers can be redeemed by different email addresses. Pros: fits sponsor-controlled flow. Cons: we need to decide tax/accounting treatment (is this revenue or promotional expense for them?) and we must ensure voucher expiry/usage limits are clear.

3) Convert to a short-term Reserved Discount (e.g., 6-month reserved -> equivalent $ value applied as a committed discount on Dedicated capacity). Pros: clean accounting for us and reserves capacity; easier to measure SLO impact. Cons: longer lifecycle, needs billing/finance sign-off and legal addendum for conversion.

Given timeline, my recommendation: pursue option #2 (sponsored vouchers) as the fast path for the demo, and prepare option #3 (reserved discount conversion) as a higher-assurance path for the contract. For either option we should require a one-off addendum that clarifies transferability, sponsor rights, and expiration.

I've attached the latest pricing playbook snippet for voucher rules. If Legal confirms scope, I can sketch the revenue-impact numbers for a 30% one-time conversion discount if the sponsor wants capacity conversion instead of pure credits.

Neha / Ben,

Quick legal note after a brief scan: we can't allow unilateral sponsor control over credits without an addendum. Reasons: assignment/transferability language in the MSA disallows third-party beneficiaries in most cases; voucher-based flows are okay if the sponsor is explicitly listed as the purchaser and we limit transferability in the voucher terms.

Suggested path:
- For demo: implement sponsored voucher flow with contract language in the voucher T&Cs that prevents resale and caps per-recipient redemption. This keeps things operationally simple and avoids MSA edits.
- For any conversion to reserved capacity or a longer-lived instrument: require a short addendum to the MSA (1-2 pages). Key clauses to include: limited assignment, sponsor indemnity for misuse, expiration & revocation rights, and accounting designation (promo vs payment).

I'll draft a 1-page addendum redline we can present to SeedForge. Also attaching a redline snippet showing the clauses we'll need.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

John / Leah — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Short update and recommended next steps so we can close before your demo Thursday: 

Proposed short-term pilot (fast path):
- Create a Sponsor Voucher pool (voucher codes purchased/issued to sponsor) that founders can redeem individually. Voucher has per-recipient cap and 6-month expiry.
- Voucher will include T&Cs we draft (no resale, no transfer beyond redemption, revocation rights). Legal will produce a 1-page addendum if SeedForge prefers the sponsor to appear on the contract.
- Ops will provision the voucher pool and provide a single management dashboard for sponsor visibility.

Longer-term / higher-assurance option:
- Convert sponsor value into a Reserved Discount Voucher tied to Dedicated capacity for a defined window (6 months). This requires finance/legal sign-off and a short MSA addendum; Ben will model revenue impact if SeedForge prefers this route.

Requests / ask list:
1) John/Leah: Please confirm you are happy to proceed with the voucher pilot and whether the sponsor wants (A) simple voucher codes they distribute, or (B) a managed dashboard where Redwood issues codes on sponsor instruction.
2) Ben: please confirm the one-time conversion discount number (Ben suggested 30% earlier as a placeholder).
3) Laura: please share the 1-page addendum draft by EOD so we can include it in the demo packet.
4) Marissa: please create an ops checklist for voucher creation + sponsor dashboard needs; include tracking for redemption rates.

If you confirm (A) for the pilot, we can have vouchers live within 48 hours. If you prefer the reserved conversion path, we'll need sign-off but can still surface a timeline in the demo.

John — happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call if that helps.
